input.question: What makes certain foods cancerous?
input.ground_truth: It depends on the chemical composition of the food or seasonings and ingredients used. For example cured meat. Cured meat or processed meat contains sodium nitrite. The heat when cooking allow sodium nitrate to react with the amines in the meat to form N - nitrosocompounds which is carcinogenic. Fatty foods. Fried food contains oil which can undergo lipid peroxidation when exposed to oxygen to form free radicals that can damage cells and their components like DNA which may have a role in cancer development. It is best to avoid consuming lots of fried street food as more free radicals are formed in reused oil. Foods that start to give off odour should also be avoided because the rancid smell indicates lipid peroxidation. It is good to consume plenty of fruits and vegetables (especially colourful ones) that are rich in antioxidants to prevent cell damage from free radicals. Source: food science major.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What makes certain foods cancerous?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Let’s imagine foods are like toys. Most toys are safe to play with, but some toys can be broken or have yucky stuff that isn’t good for you.

Now, foods are not really “cancerous” by themselves. But some foods, if we eat them in the wrong way or too much, can have things in them that might hurt our bodies over a long, long time. For example:

- Some foods can have things called “chemicals” that are not good for us if we eat too much of them. Like, if you eat too much of something called “processed meat” (like hot dogs or bacon every single day), some scientists think it might make it a little bit more likely for someone to get sick with cancer when they grow up.
- Some foods can be cooked in a way that makes them have “bad stuff” in them. Like, if you burn food too much when you cook it, it can make something called “heterocyclic amines,” which some studies say might not be good for us if we eat them a lot.
- Some foods have things called “preservatives” or “additives” that help them last longer, but too many of those might not be good for us in very big amounts.

But here’s the important part: **No food is “cancerous” by itself.** It’s when we eat certain foods in the wrong way, or too much of them, or mix them with other unhealthy things, that it can sometimes be a problem for our bodies over a very long time.

So, it’s like: eating a little bit of something not-so-good is usually okay, but eating a lot of it every day for many years can sometimes make it harder for your body to stay healthy. That’s why grown-ups say to eat lots of fruits and vegetables, and not too much of the not-so-good stuff!
